about: The 270 practices read in the TAOM repository on 2026-11-13, each with the mapper's verdict, the skeptic's outcome and the final verdict. See adopt-taom-2026-11-13.md. status: ALREADY / PARTIAL / MISSING in LEVI-Achaea when read. final: ADOPT_NOW, ADOPT_PLANNED, LATER, REJECT. form: the proposed LEVI-Achaea form (a proposal by a reader, not a decision). taom_evidence: paths in the TAOM repository. <parent> is the folder that holds LEVI-Achaea.

rows.name: Narrowest-trigger routing ladder (one home per fact)
rows.form: Write docs/adrs/002-knowledge-delivery-tiers.md and replace CLAUDE.md 'Documentation-First' homes list (lines 38-42) and 'Documentation Requirements' (3872-3894) with one ladder whose every rung names a home that exists today: 1 machine-checkable: a gate in tools/ plus one line; 2 every-task rule: CLAUDE.md core; 3 game fact: its kb/ page; 4 class or system detail: .claude/classes/<class>.md or .claude/projects/<system>/ only, never a CLAUDE.md section; 5 procedure: the owning doc today, the skill once item 6 shows project skills load; 6 lesson: .claude/AGENTS.md (the existing titled archive) until item 9 moves it; 7 release history: CHANGELOG.md only; 8 memory: unchanged until the user approves item 10. In the same change, with the user's approval, reword the memory file documentation-first.md and drop the 'this file + .claude/AGENTS.md' double home at CLAUDE.md:40.
rows.reason: CLAUDE.md grew from 72 KB in June to 450 KB, and its own rule sends each fact to five stores. The ladder removes the cause of growth. Source confirmed in ADR-011 and TAOM CLAUDE.md:29-49.
rows.skeptic_reason: The idea stands: CLAUDE.md is 450,746 B today against 72,024 B on 2026-06-01 and 396,657 B on 2026-11-01, and 39 of the 77 commits since 2026-11-01 touched it. The form is wrong in three places. (1) Two rungs name homes that do not exist or do not load: there is no lessons file (docs/ holds only adrs, ai-includes, plans, reviews), and none of the 14 skills under LEVI-Achaea/.claude/skills is listed in a session started from the parent folder. A ladder that points at a missing home sends the fact back to CLAUDE.md. (2) The mapper says the rule 'sends each fact to five stores'. It does not: CLAUDE.md:38-42 routes by fact type. The real double homes are line 40 ('this file' plus .claude/AGENTS.md) and the memory file, which the memory rule documentation-first.md also names ('and the matching memory file'). (3) The largest cause of size is feature detail in the always-read file: the Mnemosyne section alone is 180,468 B (40%), so the rung for system detail matters most and should name .claude/projects/<system>/ as the only home.

rows.name: Three-file entry split: constitution, orientation, client layer
rows.form: As proposed, plus: (1) give every part of .claude/AGENTS.md a named destination before the root file is created: lines 3-149 and 259-1153 (titled lessons) to the lessons home of item 9; lines 150-258 (quick references, header template, key files) to orientation.md or the class docs; line 1154 hook table deleted (item 12). Then delete .claude/AGENTS.md so only one AGENTS.md exists. (2) Update every tracked citation of .claude/AGENTS.md in CLAUDE.md, .claude/agents/offense-system.md, .claude/agents/team-class-offense.md, .claude/skills/codex-verify/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/deep-review/SKILL.md and docs/ai-includes/agent-teams.md. (3) Do not start until the item 6 probe shows that a nested LEVI-Achaea/CLAUDE.md and its @-imports load from the parent folder, or the user moves the session folder.
rows.reason: Neither file is a small constitution today, and .claude/AGENTS.md sits where no client loads it by itself. Source sizes confirmed: 7,362 B, 5,403 B and 6,477 B. Worth doing, but as part of the migration.
rows.skeptic_reason: The split is supported by the source (CLAUDE.md 6,477 B, AGENTS.md 7,362 B, orientation.md 5,403 B, read today) and nothing like it exists in the target (no root AGENTS.md, no @-import, docs/ai-includes holds only agent-teams.md). Codex is a real second client here (skills codex-verify and review-codex), so a provider-neutral root file has a reader. The form misreads .claude/AGENTS.md. It is not only pitfalls: lines 150-258 are quick references (Before Coding Offensive/Defensive Systems, Combat Systems Quick Reference, lock tables, Code Header Template, Setup Wizard conventions, Key Files Reference) and line 1154 is a hook table. The form also leaves two files named AGENTS.md and does not update the tracked files that cite .claude/AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md 4 times, 2 agents, 2 skills, docs/ai-includes/agent-teams.md 8 times). Whether @-imports in a nested CLAUDE.md resolve when the session folder is the parent is unverified, as the mapper says.

rows.name: Context budget constants enforced by the doc linter
rows.form: Extend tools/check_context_budget.py (from item 3) with absolute caps as constants: entry docs together, 200 lines per entry file, table row 400 chars, prose line 600 chars, and `--json` for live sizes. Add tools/test_check_context_budget.py, a build.yml step and a line in .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md. Each cap lands report-only behind a STRICT_* flag, as tools/check_orphans.py does, and turns strict when the migration brings the files under it.
rows.reason: Stdlib Python fits the tools/ pattern and the repo already lands checks report-only. Absolute caps only have meaning after the file is shrunk. Source constants confirmed in lint_docs.py:47-76.
rows.skeptic_reason: Weaker benefit than stated until the migration is far along. The TAOM caps are 22,528 B for the entry docs and 200 lines per file; the target file is 450,746 B and 3,901 lines, twenty times over, with 82 lines over 600 characters (measured). A report-only check prints the same long list on every run and gates nothing, and the mapper's own reason says absolute caps 'only have meaning after the file is shrunk'. Item 3's committed ceiling, lowered after each extraction, reaches the same end state with one number. The 200-line figure is the Claude Code guidance for files loaded at launch, and whether the nested CLAUDE.md loads at launch from the parent folder is not known. Move to LATER: add the absolute caps and the line caps when item 1 (the split) lands and the entry files are within reach of them.

rows.name: Grow-only ratchet for files already over their cap
rows.form: Create tools/check_context_budget.py (stdlib) with tools/context_budget.json holding ceilings for CLAUDE.md and .claude/AGENTS.md at today's LF-folded byte counts, tools/test_check_context_budget.py, a build.yml step, a line in .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md step 5 and a line in the CONTRIBUTING.md CI list. A missing file is a finding; --update only lowers. Land report-only behind a STRICT_* flag. Turn strict only when (a) the item 0 ladder is in CLAUDE.md and every rung names an existing home, and (b) the check runs before the push to main (the /verify list at least, the item 4 git hook when it exists). Re-run after a rebase. Lower the ceiling in the same commit as each extraction.
rows.reason: The file gained about 54 KB in 13 days. A committed ceiling is fast, deterministic and the same on Windows and CI. In TAOM the ratchet compares path rules with HEAD; using it on the entry file is an adaptation.
rows.skeptic_reason: I could not overturn the idea. No size check exists in tools/ or build.yml. The growth is real (54,089 B in 13 days). *.md is eol=lf in .gitattributes, so the byte count is the same on Windows and CI. The source supports both halves of the adaptation: lint_docs.py:1083-1095 gates growth over HEAD, and check_doc_graph_ratchet.py uses a committed JSON baseline. Two points of the form must change. (1) The strict trigger is too early. With ceilings on both CLAUDE.md and .claude/AGENTS.md and no lessons file yet, a new pitfall has no legal home on the day the check turns strict, so the gate blocks true work. (2) CI runs only after the push to main, so a strict failure found there blocks the release tag. The check must run before the push. The form also omits CONTRIBUTING.md, which lists the CI steps by number (documentation-first rule).

rows.name: Budget gate that binds every committer, on the staged tree
rows.form: Create .githooks/pre-commit (POSIX sh, fails open with a message, skips WindowsApps python aliases) and tools/test_githooks_pre_commit.py. It runs only fast checks on the staged tree: check_context_budget.py; the three-file version match, only when one of version.txt, muddler_project/mfile or src_new/scripts/_groups.yaml is staged; and a Lua 5.1 loadstring check through lupa of each staged .lua file, read with `git show :<path>` and passed whole (no header stripping, the same input CI gives luac5.1 -p). If lupa is missing, say the syntax check did not run and allow the commit. The user runs `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` once; worktrees share the setting and each uses its own branch's copy. kb_*.py --check steps stay in /verify and CI. Land each check report-only for a week of commits, then let exit 1 refuse.
rows.reason: The Claude hooks sit in a folder sessions do not start in and read $TOOL_INPUT, so nothing checks a commit before main. A git hook works for every client and worktree. Source confirmed in .githooks/pre-commit.
rows.skeptic_reason: I could not overturn it. No .githooks folder exists and core.hooksPath is unset. The three Claude hooks that should gate a commit read $TOOL_INPUT, while Claude Code delivers tool input on stdin (TAOM harness-facts.md:28, DOC-sourced), and they are wired in LEVI-Achaea/.claude/settings.local.json, which is not the session folder's settings. So no check runs before a commit. `python` on PATH is /c/Python314/python and imports lupa.lua51 and yaml (run today); `python3` is the WindowsApps alias, which the source hook already skips. The form has one misreading: source Lua files do not carry a YAML header to strip. They open with a Lua block comment (`--[[mudlet`), and CI runs `luac5.1 -p` on the raw file. The stripping in lint-before-commit.sh is a leftover. Two more corrections: check the staged blob, not the working copy, because sessions share a tree; and there is no working Claude gate to run beside for two weeks.

rows.name: Trap sheets: path-scoped one-line trap tables plus a capped index
rows.form: Create .claude/rules/traps/ with path-scoped sheets: triggers.md (src_new/triggers/**), tests.md (src_new/tests/**), basher.md and mnemosyne.md (their script and trigger folders), release.md (version.txt, muddler_project/mfile, CHANGELOG.md, build.sh, .github/**), kb-tools.md (tools/kb_*.py, tools/sim/**, kb/**). Each row: trap, the never-do, a link to the owning lesson or doc. The always-read index keeps traps about the live profile, OneDrive and sysupdate.
rows.reason: The pitfalls sit in a file nothing loads and in the always-read file. Path scoping is the right trigger, but its loading is unverified for this folder layout. Source confirmed in traps/mission.md and orientation.md.
rows.skeptic_reason: The mechanism is unproven here and the evidence at hand points against it. Sessions start in the parent folder, and a session started there lists none of the 14 skills under LEVI-Achaea/.claude/skills, so nested .claude content is not being discovered. TAOM's own harness fact says rule patterns are relative to the directory that holds the rule's .claude folder and that a rule does not load for a sibling worktree unless Claude starts there; here every lv-* worktree is a sibling. If the sheets do not load, moving the pitfalls out of CLAUDE.md removes them from every agent's view, which is worse than today. The item also rests on three things not built (item 6 probe, item 9 link targets, item 0 ladder) and on a user decision about the session folder. The mapper gave the same reason for putting item 13 (skills) at LATER; rules deserve the same step. Move to LATER: reconsider when the probe shows a path rule in LEVI-Achaea/.claude/rules loads from the parent folder and from an lv-* worktree.

rows.name: Sourced, dated harness-facts rules
rows.form: Create docs/reference/harness-facts.md: a Fact, Source, Why table where each source is DOC (URL, date), EMPIRICAL (where, when) or UNVERIFIED. First rows: what loads when the session folder is the parent Achaea folder (nested CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules, skills, settings.local.json hooks); hook input arrives on stdin; a relative autoMemoryDirectory is ignored; the skill key is `user-invocable`. Copy a TAOM row only after a re-check here. Replace the CLAUDE.md Hooks section with a link.
rows.reason: The target harness rests on untested beliefs. TAOM's rows name two of its faults exactly: tool input arrives on stdin, and a relative autoMemoryDirectory is silently ignored. None of the 14 project skills is listed in this session.
rows.skeptic_reason: I tried four attacks and none held. (a) Exists: a search of CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/ai-includes/agent-teams.md and the tooling-review skill for stdin, /compact, Explore, session folder or a Claude docs URL found nothing; the tooling-review skill reviews updates and records no facts. (b) Constraint: it is a docs-only file, and the probes are the user's, which the mapper lists. (c) Source: the three TAOM rows the mapper leans on are there and are DOC-sourced (stdin at harness-facts.md:28; relative autoMemoryDirectory ignored in harness-loading.md; `user-invocable` in the allowlist at harness-skills-agents.md:21). (d) Cost: each of the named target faults is real and checked today: three hooks read $TOOL_INPUT; <parent>/.claude/settings.json holds the relative value '.claude/memory' and that folder holds 18 files dated March to July while the live memory is under ~/.claude/projects; three skills use `user_invocable`. One note for the writer: `user_invocable: true` is harmless because true is the default, so record it as a typo, not a fault. The hook-table replacement overlaps item 12; do it once there.

rows.name: Delivery map in CLAUDE.md, with its blind spots named
rows.form: Add a short 'How your context is delivered' section near the top of CLAUDE.md, written from docs/reference/harness-facts.md: what loads at launch from the parent folder, what loads on the first read inside LEVI-Achaea, what a subagent and Explore get, what survives /compact, that memory is machine-local, and that no rule reaches the live Mudlet profile, <profile>/fightlogs or the OneDrive inbox, so the kb-ingest and fight-log procedures carry their own traps.
rows.reason: Five bullets, cheap once the facts are known. The parent-folder start makes the blind spots larger here than in TAOM, but the text must follow item 6. Source confirmed in TAOM CLAUDE.md:12-27.
rows.skeptic_reason: Checked for an existing section: CLAUDE.md has no delivery heading and no text on /compact, Explore or what a subagent loads (grep found only the custom-subagent list at line 427). The blind spots are real here: the session folder is not the repo, kbcapture and fightlog write to the Mudlet profile, and the inbox is a OneDrive file (CLAUDE.md:17-30). The cost is five bullets. The mapper already orders it after the item 6 probes and the user's session-folder decision, which answers the only real risk (guesses stated as facts). If the user chooses a parent-folder CLAUDE.md, the map belongs in that file; the mapper's dependency covers this.

rows.name: Migration order for shrinking a large CLAUDE.md
rows.form: Write docs/plans/claude-md-migration.md with stop-anywhere phases. Mark each phase with what it needs: 1 copy the memory folder and record sizes (docs-only); 2 ADR-002 (docs-only); 3 owners for each CLAUDE.md section, one section per commit: first a small pilot section (for example Gear Audit, 3.5 KB) to prove the re-read step, then Mnemosyne (180 KB, three copies: CLAUDE.md, .claude/projects/mnemosyne, memory/mnemosyne.md; the code is the judge), then ataxiaBasher (37 KB); 4 split the entry files, after the session-folder decision; 5 gates (tools/ and build.yml, CI steps run locally first; no version bump); 6 memory (user approval, outside git); 7 hooks (user edits settings); 8 rules and lessons. After each move, re-read every compressed row against its owner and the code, and lower the item 3 ceiling in the same commit.
rows.reason: A one-time trim regrew in TAOM (ADR-011 Alternative 1). The target already has owners for most of the content, so the order applies, but it is several days of work. RCA F11 and F18 confirm the re-read step.
rows.skeptic_reason: The order is supported by the source (ADR-011 phases; the 2026-08-05 trim regrew) and the target has owners for the largest block: the Mnemosyne section is 180,468 B of 450,746 B, and .claude/projects/mnemosyne already has 8 files. Two points of the form are wrong. (1) 'All docs-only' is false: the gates phase edits tools/ and .github/workflows/build.yml, the hooks phase changes wiring in a guarded settings file and needs the user, and the memory phase edits a folder outside git and needs the user's approval. (2) The largest section has three copies to reconcile against the code, not two: the CLAUDE.md section, .claude/projects/mnemosyne, and memory/mnemosyne.md (203,843 B). That is the highest-risk move, so it should follow a small pilot.

rows.name: Lessons archive: grep-first evidence, one-line promotion into the area rule
rows.form: Step 1 (docs-only, no rewrite): `git mv` the lesson part of .claude/AGENTS.md (lines 3-149 and 259-1153) to docs/lessons/lessons.md with titles and text verbatim, and write docs/lessons/README.md: list headings with Grep on '^## ', read matching entries, name them in the plan; before appending, grep for the root cause and add a new instance under the existing entry. New entries use `## rule (version)`, Why missed, Prevent, Source; old entries stay as written. Update the citations in CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills/deep-review/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/codex-verify/SKILL.md. Step 2 (user approval, item 10): append memory bug-patterns.md and CLAUDE.md 'Lessons Learned' (10,320 B), merging only exact duplicates. Split into category files only when one file makes heading search slow. Until trap sheets exist, a standing lesson is promoted as one line into the class dossier, the kb page or the CLAUDE.md core.
rows.reason: The lessons are already written as general rules with a version. They lack one home and a channel to the agent. Source confirmed in LESSONS-LEARNED.md and orientation.md:24-27.
rows.skeptic_reason: Most of the archive already exists, so the proposed hand-merge into seven category files costs more than it gives. .claude/AGENTS.md lines 259-1153 are about 50 titled, versioned lessons written as general rules, and memory/bug-patterns.md adds 134,122 B with dated headings. Rewriting both into a four-field shape and sorting them into seven files by hand is where a qualifier is lost (the mapper's own risk, and TAOM's RCA F11/F18). The promotion channel the practice depends on is the trap sheet, which I moved to LATER (item 5), so for now the archive is reached only by grep; that is still better than a file nothing names. The source supports grep-first use (LESSONS-LEARNED.md 'How to use').

rows.name: Memory holds resume cards only; durable rules go to the repo
rows.form: Split in two. Part A (after user approval, small): copy the user's durable rules into the repo, release-chain-discipline.md and documentation-first.md first, into the CLAUDE.md core (root AGENTS.md once item 1 exists); leave a one-line pointer in memory. Add a report-only count of `memory/<name>.md` citations in tracked files to tools/check_context_budget.py. Part B (after item 8 phase 3 has given each system an owner): fold each class or system memory file into its existing owner (.claude/classes/<class>.md, .claude/projects/<system>/) one file per commit, judged against the code, after reading it for machine paths and personal content because the repo is published. Machine-local notes (mudlet-mcp.md, onedrive-save-conflicts.md, vscode-worktree-counts.md) stay in memory. Reword CLAUDE.md:41 and 3885 and the memory rule in the same change as Part A. No nudge hook until hooks load.
rows.reason: 797 KB of durable knowledge is on one machine and outside git, and tracked files cite it by a path that is not in the repo. The user has two machines. TAOM's hook matches feedback_ file names, which the target does not use.
rows.skeptic_reason: The idea stands for the user's rules, but the form understates cost and conflict for the bulk move. (b) It reverses a standing user rule in three places: the memory rule documentation-first.md ('and the matching memory file'), CLAUDE.md:41 and CLAUDE.md:3885. The mapper lists approval, but the form should not bundle the low-risk part with the high-risk part. (d) The class and system files are not a move: memory/mnemosyne.md (203,843 B) overlaps a 180 KB CLAUDE.md section and 8 files in .claude/projects/mnemosyne, so each file is a three-way reconciliation against the code. (e) Destination AGENTS.md does not exist at the root yet, and 'the build skill' is not loaded in parent-folder sessions. Also, origin is a GitHub repo whose releases players download, so moved text becomes public; each file needs a read for machine paths and personal notes first. The cheap, high-value part is real: release-chain-discipline.md (9,528 B) holds the release rules (no PR, tag by name, wait for main CI) only on this machine, where Codex and a second checkout cannot read them, and tracked files cite memory files 25 times (my grep; the mapper counted 26).

rows.name: Guards against a gate that silently checks nothing
rows.form: Add an 'Adding a gate' section to CONTRIBUTING.md: a gate is done when it has been shown refusing one real bad input where it runs, and a test fails when its input set is empty or its anchor is renamed. Apply it first to tools/check_context_budget.py (a missing CLAUDE.md is a finding; a crash exits 3). Then make src_new/tests/test_runner.lua exit 1 on zero test files and give the build.yml syntax step a minimum file count.
rows.reason: The repo does this in places (lupa import guard, STRICT flags), but the Lua runner reports success with no test files and two hooks pass when their input is absent. Source confirmed in lint_docs.py and hook-authoring.md:125-130.
rows.skeptic_reason: I tried to find it already present and to find the gaps overstated; neither held. The gaps are as stated: src_new/tests/test_runner.lua:118-146 prints 'No test files found', then 'All tests passed!' and exits 0; the build.yml syntax step counts files but has no floor; lint-before-commit.sh exits 0 with a warning when no luac is found; check-changelog.sh always exits 0 and writes to stderr, a channel Claude does not see. The principle exists only in pieces: the report-only rule is in the tools/check_orphans.py docstring, 'Break-back every fix' in CONTRIBUTING.md covers tests of fixes, and build.yml has one input guard (the lupa import). No place states the rule for a new gate. The source rule is confirmed at hook-authoring.md ('Prove a gate live') and lint_docs.py import-missing and trap-index-missing findings. Cost is a few lines; the floor 'more than zero' cannot fail a good run (140 files in src_new/tests today; single-file mode through tools/run_lua_tests.py still yields one). The tests folder is not read by tools/convert_to_muddler.py, so the runner change does not alter the package.

rows.name: No count that nothing computes; one source of truth per list
rows.form: One sentence in the item 0 ladder: always-read text holds no count that nothing computes, no incident story and no copy of another file's list; a count names the command that prints it, or its date. Then: delete the hook tables at CLAUDE.md:3855-3868 and .claude/AGENTS.md:1154-1165, and replace the table at CLAUDE.md:398-409 with one line pointing at .claude/settings.local.json for wiring and docs/reference/harness-facts.md (item 6) for behaviour. Replace the skill table at CLAUDE.md:411-424 with a pointer to .claude/skills/. In GETTING_STARTED.md:235 and README.md:952 drop the '1800+' figure from the tree comment and state no number.
rows.reason: Two hook tables in CLAUDE.md already disagree (5 scripts against 8). The fix is deletion plus a pointer, which also shrinks the file. Source confirmed in rules-catalog.md and RCA F4, F22.
rows.skeptic_reason: The idea stands and the drift is real, but the form misses one copy and misjudges two cases. (1) There are three hook lists, not two: CLAUDE.md:398-409 (8 scripts, which matches settings.local.json today), CLAUDE.md:3855-3868 (5 scripts plus inline) and .claude/AGENTS.md:1154-1165 (3 scripts plus inline). (2) README.md and GETTING_STARTED.md are player-facing pages, not always-read agent text, and '1800+' is still a true floor (2,280 files under src_new/triggers today). Restating a number there creates the next stale count; remove the number. (3) Item 6 also replaces the Hooks section with a link, so the two items must agree on one pointer. The skill table claim is confirmed: 11 rows against 14 skill folders.

rows.name: Skill descriptions carry trigger and gate; CLAUDE.md lists only the rest
rows.form: After the skills load in sessions: rewrite each description in .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md as trigger plus gate (verify: 'before any push to main: run every validate step of build.yml'), change `user_invocable` to `user-invocable` in build, kb-ingest and version-bump, and add tools/test_claude_config.py with a frontmatter key allowlist and a name-equals-folder check. Cut the CLAUDE.md skill table to the reflex gates.
rows.reason: Descriptions are already short, and none of the 14 skills is listed in this session, so the description channel carries nothing today. Fix loading and the stale commands first.
rows.skeptic_reason: LATER is right. A session started from the parent folder lists none of the 14 project skills, so a description rewrite reaches no agent today. The one quick fix inside it, `user_invocable` to `user-invocable` in three skills, changes nothing because the value is true and true is the default. The descriptions are already 8 to 25 words. The more urgent fault in the skills is the stale `lua5.1` command in five of them, which item 15 covers. Nothing here is high value at low cost before skills load.

rows.name: Context budget scan and dated baseline doc
rows.form: No separate scan script. `tools/check_context_budget.py --json` (items 2 and 3) prints the live sizes, and docs/adrs/002-knowledge-delivery-tiers.md records one dated table of CLAUDE.md, .claude/AGENTS.md, MEMORY.md and skill-description sizes as phase 1 of the migration.
rows.reason: A long bash scanner and a baseline doc to keep current cost more than they give a solo maintainer while one file is the whole problem. TAOM's own baseline drifted threefold.
rows.skeptic_reason: REJECT is right. The source scan is a 29,835-byte bash script built for many rules, skills, plugins and MCP servers; here one file is the whole problem (CLAUDE.md 450,746 B, with no rules folder). The item 3 check with --json and one dated table in the ADR give the same numbers. Git Bash on this machine also lacks jq, which makes a long shell scanner a poor fit.

rows.name: Rule-text drift checks (instructions must name things that exist)
rows.form: Create tools/check_doc_refs.py with tools/test_check_doc_refs.py, report-only behind STRICT_* flags. Scope first: .claude/skills/**, .claude/agents/**, CONTRIBUTING.md, kb/README.md. Checks: (a) a backticked path that contains a slash and starts with a tracked top-level folder must be in `git ls-files`; short-form names are not judged; (b) in .claude/skills and .claude/agents only, a command line may not start with bare `lua5.1`, `luac5.1` or `python3`, unless the line carries an exemption marker (for text about CI); (c) no `memory/<name>.md` citation. Exempt kb/raw, generated pages and CHANGELOG.md. Fix the five skills in the same change so (b) starts clean, then turn it strict and add the build.yml step and the CONTRIBUTING.md CI line. Add CLAUDE.md to the scope after item 8. Leave the line-anchor check out; the audit method in documentation-first.md (git log -S) is the tool for moved citations.
rows.reason: The repo's own audit found moved citations with no check, and instruction files name a command this machine lacks. The path-exists part has near-zero false positives. Source confirmed in lint_docs.py:1202-1260.
rows.skeptic_reason: The need is real but two of the four proposed checks would give false positives, and the scope is wrong for a first landing. (1) 'No bare lua5.1 or python3' is wrong for CONTRIBUTING.md and any text that describes CI: build.yml really runs `lua5.1 src_new/tests/test_runner.lua` and `python3 -B tools/...` on Linux. The prompt says: read-only, return the report as the final message, do not write the output path, and carries the project rules until a root AGENTS.md exists. Add `docs/reviews/raw/` to .gitignore. Before the worktree is removed, save the verified assessment to tracked docs/reviews/. Replace `lua5.1` with `/c/Python314/python tools/run_lua_tests.py`. Run the command once by hand before the skill text is trusted.
rows.reason: Source confirmed. Both target skills depend on the plugin's /codex:* slash commands and on stream polling, and one names a test command this machine lacks. The CLI is installed and this path is already trusted.
rows.skeptic_reason: The idea stands: the target skills tell Codex to write the report file itself (the failure the source records for 2026-09-13), poll with Monitor, and name `lua5.1`. `codex` runs from Git Bash here (codex-cli 0.153.4). Four points of the form are wrong or missing. (1) 'Run from LEVI-Achaea' misses the target's worktree rule: unmerged work lives in a sibling lv-* folder, and the source says 'Reviewing a worktree: dispatch from the worktree itself'. Dispatching from the main checkout reviews main, not the change, and that tree may be on another session's branch. (2) The source gets its sandbox from a project .codex/config.toml (`workspace-write`); the target has no such file and the user config sets no sandbox mode. `codex exec` supports `-s read-only`; pass it explicitly because several sessions share the tree. (3) An ignored docs/reviews/raw/ inside a worktree is deleted with the worktree; the verified summary must be saved to tracked docs/reviews/ first. (4) The source has no codex-verify skill; rewriting two skills creates two dispatch contracts. The existing plugin path (/codex:rescue, plugin 1.0.2 is installed) can stay as the stated fallback.

So the idea stands, with three corrections. rows.name: Mandatory RCA for every confirmed finding, with a lesson ledger and escalation
rows.form: Adapt, do not copy. Write docs/reviews/rca-<topic>-<date>.md only for a bug found in live play or a confirmed HIGH; for the rest, add one row `Bug | Category | Why missed | Prevent` to that version's CHANGELOG.md entry. Each systemic lesson goes once into the single ledger (grep first). A repeat must become a test or a tools/check_*.py check landed report-only. Categories: timing, trigger pattern, state reset, game-mechanic assumption, test that cannot fail.

Lessons with a why-missed account are written today in four places: CHANGELOG.md (89 lines with why-missed or break-back wording), .claude/AGENTS.md (dated 'learned the hard way' headings, each a rule with its version), CLAUDE.md (for example 'Silent gates: four rules from the 2026-08-19 Grulk death'), and memory/bug-patterns.md (134 KB). The August Codex review already carries 'Why it was missed' per finding. Escalation of a repeat into a check has happened without an RCA rule: tools/check_wrap.py was written after three wrapped-trigger bugs in one week, and check_orphans has three STRICT flags turned on after report-only runs. So the missing piece is one sentence (a repeat must become a test or a report-only tools/check_*.py), not a document type. The proposed form adds a fifth lesson store plus table rows in a 1.5 MB CHANGELOG.md, and depends on a ledger consolidation in another lane that is not decided. The source's case rests on 644 RCA files and a hook that lints them; the target has neither the volume nor the hook, and hook wiring needs the user. Move to LATER, behind the single-ledger decision. The one-sentence repeat rule can go into CONTRIBUTING.md 'Break-back every fix' now.

rows.name: Completeness lens: no gate silenced, two-edit test check, spec check
rows.form: One report-only command, written once in .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md step 5 (CI parity) and referenced from CLAUDE.md's merge-to-main step 2 and from deep-review's completeness block: `git -C <worktree> diff $(git -C <worktree> merge-base HEAD origin/main) -U0 -- src_new/tests tools | grep -nE '^-\s*it\(|^-\s*def test_|^\+.*(ALLOWLIST|NEVER_RUN|MUDLET_API)|^\+\s*STRICT_[A-Z_]+ = False'`, plus `git -C <worktree> diff --stat <merge-base> -- tools/sim/gates_whole.json tools/kb_replay.py tools/test_kb_replay.py` (any change to the RULES block or to the freeze test is a hit). Each hit needs a stated reason in the CHANGELOG entry; never blocking. Keep the break-back question (name the decision whose inversion leaves every test green; CONTRIBUTING.md:72 and AGENTS.md:1067 already state the rule) and the spec check against the user's request.

rows.skeptic_reason: The check is cheap, report-only and fits the repo's pattern, and source lens 4 reads as claimed (item 8 with a ready grep, item 9 two-edit check, item 10 spec check). But the form misreads the target in four places. (1) 'Protected only by prose' is partly wrong: the RULES constants have a freeze test (tools/test_kb_replay.py:552 `test_the_frozen_thresholds_have_not_moved`) and check_wrap.py fails on a stale ALLOWLIST entry. The real hole is that the test can be edited in the same diff, and that tools/sim/gates_whole.json has no freeze test at all. (2) The pattern covers only Lua `it(` removals; half the gates are Python unittest files (tools/test_*.py), so removed `def test_` lines must be in it. (3) Sessions start in the non-git parent folder, so the command needs `git -C <worktree>`. (4) Neither /verify nor /deep-review was invoked in 36 sessions; the path every version takes is the local CI run in CLAUDE.md's merge-to-main steps (line 334-337).

rows.name: Bound-surface snapshot with an offline binding gate and a human residue list
rows.form: tools/kb_trigger_evidence.py, report-only: import patterns() from tools/check_wrap.py (it reads folded patterns); judge type 0 as substring, 1 as regex, 2 as line-start, 3 as exact; list types 4-7 under 'not judged'; count a regex Python cannot compile as unparsed. Input: tracked kb/raw/logs/*.txt, kb/raw/logs/ours/*.log and kb/raw/live only. Output sorted, LF, UTF-8: kb/mechanics/trigger-evidence.json and .md (pattern, type, match count, first file and row). Staleness by a hash of inputs as kb_rules.py does (sha256 with CRLF normalised), not by regeneration; keep it out of build.yml until the report is clean. The stated check is 'a pattern that had evidence and now has none'. CONFLICTS rows that say the line is uncaptured remain the human list.
rows.reason: Source confirmed. Target tests real patterns only for chosen triggers; missing captures are tracked by hand in CONFLICTS (rows 1, 5, 29). A silent non-firing trigger is the stated signature failure.
rows.skeptic_reason: I tried to overturn it on cost and on benefit and measured both in memory (read-only). A sample of 150 of the 2,625 regex patterns over 158,947 unique lines from kb/raw/logs and kb/raw/live took 19 s, so a naive full run is about 5.5 minutes; 48 of 150 (32%) had a matching line; only 4 regex patterns fail to compile in Python re. So the report is feasible and about one third of patterns get evidence, but the form has four faults. (1) 'read every - pattern:' with a one-line reader finds 4,036 of 4,363 patterns; 327 are folded over two YAML lines, the same fault check_wrap.py fixed in v4.7.436. (2) Patterns are not all regex: types 0, 2 and 3 are substring, line-start and exact; types 4, 5, 6 and 7 (296 patterns: Lua function, line spacer, colour, prompt) cannot be judged against text and are not 'unparsed'. (3) kb/raw/logs holds untracked .html copies of the same logs next to the .txt imports; reading both doubles the work. (4) A --check that regenerates would add minutes to every push in a repo that releases six times a day. The source gate resolves 100% of bindings against the installed game; here 68% stay UNPROVEN, so the useful signal is a pattern that goes from PROVEN to UNPROVEN after an edit, not the UNPROVEN list.

rows.form: Edit LEVI-Achaea/.gitattributes: add 'kb/raw/** text eol=lf' and '*.txt text eol=lf' (the *.log and *.wiki files are all under kb/raw, so no separate rules), a reason comment per block (raw evidence is read by generators that must be byte-identical on Windows and Linux; line endings are the one thing kb-ingest may change), a note that merge=union is deliberately not used for CHANGELOG.md and why, and a dated verify line that tests index and attribute only: 'git ls-files --eol kb/raw' must show i/lf and attr/text eol=lf on every row; w/crlf in an old checkout is expected. Two corrections. (1) The dated verify line cannot be the source's 'want w/lf on every row': this checkout has 5,823 w/crlf files and the mapper rightly forbids a renormalize or re-checkout in a shared tree, so that check would fail on day one and for good. The benefit is that new worktrees and clones get LF and that a future byte-reading generator cannot differ between Windows and Linux. (e) The claim 'PreToolUse matchers are Bash only, so PowerShell commands pass every git gate' is true of the matcher but misses the larger facts: the hooks are wired in the nested LEVI-Achaea/.claude/settings.local.json while sessions start in the parent folder, whose settings.json has no hooks, and block-git-bypass.sh:7, lint-before-commit.sh:6 and protect-config.sh:5 read the variable $TOOL_INPUT, not the JSON on stdin (check-changelog.sh and log-permission-denied.sh read stdin). The doc must first state whether any gate fires for Bash at all; writing only the matcher gap would imply the Bash gates work. (e) The PowerShell 5.1 mojibake trap needs scoping: the tool in this environment runs PowerShell 7 (pwsh), which reads UTF-8; the trap applies when 'powershell' is called by name, as the two allowlisted 'powershell -Command' entries in settings.local.json do. (e) Linking from CLAUDE.md alone does not surface it: CLAUDE.md is nested below the session folder; MEMORY.md is the index loaded at session start.

The by-name readers are mostly loud already (kb --check gates go stale when a read Lua file changes), and a hand-kept register would be one more parallel doc. tools/ has no test_kb_prio_diff.py, which confirms the one gap, but a test for a tool that runs only on a pasted priority list is not high value.

The package is generated from YAML-header Lua files by tools/convert_to_muddler.py, so a stray sidecar is not copied verbatim.
rows.reason: No tracked backup sidecar exists (git ls-files finds none) and no packaging incident is recorded. The source problem came from a build that copies a folder verbatim, which the target does not do.
rows.skeptic_reason: REJECT is correct, and I closed the mapper's open point: convert_to_muddler.py collects sources with rglob('*.lua') only, so a stray sidecar is not packaged, and git ls-files finds no .bak, .orig, .old, .tmp, .rej or ~ file.
